Excisional wound healing (secondary intention and biopsy sites)

Animal wound models dominate the category; two oral-biopsy randomized trials provide limited clinical evidence, including a recent sham-controlled null study.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Animal wound models dominate the category; two oral-biopsy randomized trials provide limited clinical evidence, including a recent sham-controlled null study.

Summary of the Evidence

There are 131 unique titles across two database categories: 129 excision or secondary-intention wound models and two human oral-biopsy trials. The biopsy studies concern a related mucosal wound but are not direct replications of cutaneous secondary-intention healing. Five publications carry in-vitro or ex-vivo tags that overlap animal studies. (Collado-Murcia et al. 2026)

Human and clinical evidence

Two randomized clinical reports address oral biopsy sites. The 2026 sham-controlled study included 62 patients and found no clear added benefit for postoperative pain or inflammation over the short follow-up. These findings are site-specific and do not establish effects on chronic, larger, or cutaneous wounds. No larger independent human cohort is indexed in these two biopsy records.

Animal evidence

The 129 excision-model titles include 83 rat and 26 mouse records, with the remainder across other species. Five records also carry in-vitro tags. These experiments investigate wound area, closure, histology, collagen, and cellular response, with positive and null results across doses and models. They are not 129 human cohorts and should not be pooled as clinical outcome evidence.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

Five in-vitro or ex-vivo tags overlap animal-model publications in the database. No separate human tissue experiment is counted as a clinical cohort. The cell or tissue findings are mechanistic and do not resolve the mixed animal results.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The preclinical literature spans multiple light sources, wavelengths, doses, and treatment schedules. The 2026 oral-biopsy abstract does not provide a complete parameter set suitable for cross-study comparison. Wound location, depth, closure method, and disease context differ substantially, so settings should not be inferred across these models.

Interpretation

There is extensive preclinical work but little direct clinical evidence for secondary-intention healing. The two biopsy trials are adjacent evidence, and the recent study did not demonstrate a clear short-term benefit. Future trials should specify wound type, standardize aftercare, and measure blinded wound closure, pain, infection, and scar quality.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The broad category combines 129 animal excision-wound titles with two human oral-biopsy trials, which are related wound evidence rather than equivalent secondary-intention cohorts. The biopsy results are not consistently positive. Further human studies should distinguish wound types and assess closure, pain, infection, and scar outcomes.
